name: Backend & Databases
blurb: Postgres schema and query tuning, API design, auth, and the Supabase, Neon, Prisma, Stripe, Firebase and NoSQL details that bite.
searches: Supabase changelog new feature this month
PostgreSQL new release feature or performance change
Prisma ORM release notes new version
agent skill Postgres API design database Claude new

tests.prompt: Design tables for a multi-tenant invoicing app on Supabase.
tests.good: bigint identity PKs plus UUID public ids, tenant_id with composite indexes, FKs indexed, numeric or cents for money, timestamptz, RLS on every table with (select auth.uid()) and WITH CHECK on updates.

tests.prompt: Our orders list endpoint got slow at page 500.
tests.good: Asks for explain (analyze, buffers), replaces OFFSET with cursor pagination on (created_at, id), adds a matching composite index, caps limit at 100.

tests.prompt: Add Stripe subscriptions to our Next.js app.
tests.good: Uses Checkout Sessions with dynamic payment methods, verifies webhook signatures on the raw body, grants access from subscription and invoice events idempotently, pins the API version, keeps secret keys server-side.

tests.prompt: Build the API and Postgres schema for a booking app for dog groomers: salons, groomers, appointments and card deposits through Stripe. Neon for the database, Fastify for the API, deployed to Cloud Run. Give me a threat model before launch.
tests.good: States a short plan first: schema, API and payments here (postgres-schema.md, neon.md, api-design.md, stripe.md), the container and deploy through cloud-devops (docker.md and gcp.md: non-root image on 0.0.0.0:$PORT, secrets from Secret Manager, a dedicated service account), the threat model through security (threat-modeling.md: data-flow diagram and STRIDE over the booking and payment flows). Pooled Neon URL for the app, direct URL for migrations; a database constraint against double booking; deposits granted from verified webhooks, idempotent by event id; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: I'm building a small Hono API on Cloudflare Workers with a Neon Postgres database and I want to use Drizzle ORM. Set it up: a users table and a posts table (a user has many posts, posts have a title and body), the first migration, a query that returns a user with their latest 10 posts, and how I should run migrations in dev versus production. My Neon dashboard gives me both a pooled and a direct connection string.
tests.good: Defines both tables with pgTable in a TypeScript schema, with a foreign key from posts to users that has an explicit onDelete, an index on the foreign key column, NOT NULL and timestamptz columns; Adds drizzle.config.ts with dialect postgresql, schema path, out folder and the database URL read from an env var, never hard-coded; Uses drizzle-kit generate then migrate (checked-in SQL migrations) for production and states that drizzle-kit push is for local prototyping only; Runs migrations with the direct (unpooled) Neon URL and has the app use the pooled URL via the neon-http or neon-serverless driver suited to Workers, noting that neon-http has no interactive transactions; Shows the latest-10-posts query with the relational query API or a join with orderBy and limit, Version dependent: on Drizzle 0.x pass the schema (drizzle(url, { schema })) with relations() per table; on 1.0, which current docs describe, pass the defineRelations() object (drizzle(url, { relations })); Keeps secrets in wrangler secrets or .dev.vars, not in git, and applies migrations to a Neon branch or dev database before touching production, asking before running against production

tools.name: PostgreSQL
tools.why: Most-used database among developers (58.2% in Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025), first for the third year running.

tools.name: MySQL
tools.why: Second most-used database (39.6%) in Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025; no MySQL content in the guides.

tools.name: Supabase
tools.why: Recommended default full backend on Postgres; over 60 percent of new database launches by coding assistants as of June 2026 per a hosting round-up; 2,700-star official skills repo.

tools.name: Prisma ORM
tools.why: Most downloaded Node/TypeScript ORM: 55.3M npm downloads in the 30 days to 5 July 2026 (Prisma's own blog).

tools.name: Drizzle ORM
tools.why: Overtook Prisma in weekly npm downloads in May 2026 (48.1M vs 55.3M over 30 days to July; PkgPulse and Prisma sources); 35,958 GitHub stars.

tools.name: Stripe
tools.why: Default payments API for web apps; Stripe's own docs now lead with agent skills and plugins (`stripe agent setup`), and the stripe/ai repo has 1,856 stars.

tools.name: Firebase
tools.why: Google's default mobile and web BaaS; official agent-skills repo has 462 stars and a first-party MCP server in firebase-tools (4,472 stars).

tools.name: MongoDB
tools.why: Leading document database and first-party Atlas MCP server (https://mcp.mongodb.com/) listed in Anthropic's connector directory; official skills repo has 188 stars.

tools.name: Redis
tools.why: Fifth most-used database (30.7%) and the fastest-rising of the top five (+8% usage) in Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025; Redis publishes its own agent skills and MCP server.

tools.name: Neon
tools.why: Serverless Postgres with copy-on-write branching, ranked a top managed Postgres in 2026 round-ups; first-party MCP server and agent skills.

tools.name: PlanetScale
tools.why: Managed MySQL (Vitess) and Postgres with branching; first-party MCP server in Anthropic's connector directory and two official skills repos (692 and 131 stars).

tools.name: SQLite and Turso
tools.why: Third most-used database (37.5% of all respondents) in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, ahead of SQL Server, Redis and MongoDB; used locally and at the edge (Turso, D1); no coverage in the guides.

tools.name: Clerk
tools.why: Leading drop-in hosted auth for Next.js and React apps in 2026 comparisons; official skills repo with CLI-based setup.

tools.name: Better Auth
tools.why: Open-source TypeScript auth library with about 6.4M weekly npm downloads and 30k stars, the most-installed option in a 2026 comparison.

tools.name: ClickHouse
tools.why: Leading open-source column store for analytics; official skills repo has 544 stars and a first-party Cloud MCP server.

tools.name: AWS databases (DynamoDB, Aurora, RDS)
tools.why: AWS-native workloads default to RDS, Aurora and DynamoDB (RDS recommended when already deep in AWS per 2026 round-ups); AWS publishes agent plugins and MCP servers.

tools.name: Microsoft SQL Server
tools.why: Fourth most-used database (30.1%) in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, ahead of Redis and MongoDB which are both listed major; the default store for .NET shops and Azure SQL.

tools.name: Elasticsearch and OpenSearch
tools.why: Eighth most-used database (16.7%) in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, nearly three times Supabase (6%); the standard backend search engine, with an official Elastic connector in Anthropic's directory. No search craft exists to own it.

tools.name: Postman
tools.why: API platform used by over 40 million users and 500,000 organizations (Postman 2025 State of the API) with about 58% of the API-client market; official Postman connector in Anthropic's directory. Overlaps testing-qa for test runs but is the everyday tool for designing, documenting and mocking APIs.

tools.name: Auth0
tools.why: Most-deployed customer identity (CIAM) brand in 2026 comparisons, used by 58% of organizations with an identity-provider vendor per Ramp's spend data; official Auth0 connector in Anthropic's directory. The researcher left it out only for a low-star skills repo.

tools.name: Express
tools.why: Most-used backend web framework (19.9%) in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025; the guides already give Express rules.

tools.name: FastAPI
tools.why: Used by 14.8% of developers in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, up 5 points, the biggest rise among web frameworks; the guides already give FastAPI rules.

tools.name: Spring Boot
tools.why: Used by 14.7% of developers in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, the standard Java backend framework; no Java content in any guide.

tools.name: ASP.NET Core
tools.why: Used by 19.7% of developers in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, level with Express; no .NET content in any guide.

tools.name: Django
tools.why: Used by 12.6% of developers in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025 (Flask 14.4%), the main batteries-included Python backend with its own ORM, migrations and auth; only named once in auth.md.

tools.name: Message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ)
tools.why: Kafka is used by over 80% of the Fortune 100 (Confluent) and about 12% of professional developers, RabbitMQ by about 9-10%; the guides cover job queues (BullMQ, Celery, SQS) but not event streaming or brokers.

tools.name: Oracle Database
tools.why: Used by 10.6% of developers in the Stack Overflow Developer Survey 2025, more than DynamoDB (9.8%); enterprise mainstay with no guide coverage.

tools.name: Database GUI clients (DBeaver, pgAdmin, DataGrip)
tools.why: DBeaver is called the most widely used multi-database client and pgAdmin the default Postgres GUI in 2026 round-ups; everyday tools for inspecting schemas and running EXPLAIN, no API to automate.
